arguments.command:
python -c "
import parse

# Check regex patterns
p1 = parse.Parser('{:<}')
print('Left align search re:', p1._search_re.pattern)

p2 = parse.Parser('{:^}')
print('Center align search re:', p2._search_re.pattern)

p3 = parse.Parser('{:>}')
print('Right align search re:', p3._search_re.pattern)
"

raw_message.reasoning:
Interesting! The current behavior for `{:<}` and `{:^}` without suffix is to match the whole string (because `. +?` matches all characters, then ` *` matches trailing spaces). But in findall mode, it only matches one character at a time because of the non-greedy nature.
